description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, exercised as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='2022-07-1 ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width; the day is written as a bare '1' with its leading zero omitted and the field is closed by the trailing blank, which is part of the input rather than padding. LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no SELECT and opens no file, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter; its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins two things at once. First, the omitted-leading-zero tolerance on arm 1 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-INVALID-DATE, whose 88-level VALUE is X'0000000000000000' (L62). Despite its name that all-zeros token is the SUCCESS token - the SEVERITY and MSG-NO halfwords declared at L72-L73 inside CASE-1-CONDITION-ID both decode to zero, so the numeric REDEFINES views WS-SEVERITY-N (L44) and WS-MSG-NO-N (L47) written at L123 and L124 render '0000' and '0000' zero-filled to four digits, RETURN-CODE is 0, and the arm moves 'Date is valid' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) (L130), right space-padded to fifteen. The inverted condition name is preserved, not corrected. A day of '1 ' is accepted because a numeric picture token consumes digits greedily up to its declared width and stops at the first non-digit, needing only one: the '1' is taken as the day and the blank simply closes the field. A stricter reimplementation would refuse the blank and report 2520 instead, so this case is the guard against losing that tolerance. Second, the group-move corruption of WS-DATE at offset 45. L105-L106 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the declared length, hence always 10 whatever the date holds - into VSTRING-LENGTH; L107-L108 moves LS-DATE into both VSTRING-TEXT and WS-DATE, so WS-DATE briefly holds the true ten characters; and after the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116, L122 moves the whole WS-DATE-TO-TEST group into WS-DATE PIC X(10). An alphanumeric group move takes the leftmost ten bytes, which are the two-byte binary halfword X'000A' followed by only the first eight text bytes '2022-07-', so the final two characters of the input - here the day digit '1' and its closing blank - are truncated on the right. That corruption is expected output and is preserved, not repaired: the day the program accepted is invisible in the message it returns. THE TWIN: case04 is deliberately paired with case01.json, which is run with LS-DATE '2022-07-19'. The two inputs differ at character ten and nowhere else, and character ten is precisely what L122 throws away, so the 80-byte line below is BYTE-IDENTICAL to case01.json's by design. The duplication is the assertion, not a copy-paste error to be tidied: had an implementation propagated the full ten-character date into offset 45, case01 would end '2022-07-19' and this one '2022-07-1 ', and the two lines could not possibly match. Their identity is therefore positive evidence that the truncation is reproduced, and neither the inputs nor the two expectations may be differentiated. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast clean in both, because L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 summed span by span to exactly 80 bytes, the nine feedback tokens at L62-L70, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and no Language Environment services are reachable, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022-07-1 ' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
